title: Python 3 support
body: As promised, here's a pull request which adds support for Python 3. I have modified the tox.ini file to test against Python 3.3 (I have not tested with 3.0 or 3.1 or 3.2 though it should work with those as well). I also configured tox to test against Python 2.5, since you mentioned you had customers using 2.5. The unit tests seem to work with 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, pypy, and 3.3, and I tested using my account to send a test charge with 2.5 and 3.3 and it worked in both cases. The most significant change I made was to move the test directory to live within the actual stripe package itself. I didn't want to have to do this; I also like keeping unit tests separate when possible instead of bundling them as a sub-package. However, I had to do this so that tox would run tests against the proper 2to3 source code, as a workaround for this unresolved tox issue: https://code.google.com/p/pytox/issues/detail?id=21 As indicated, I'm using 2to3 in setup.py, so you can still just have one single source code base which is automatically converted on install. Let me know if you have any questions - I'll be using this for my own Python 3 project, which is in the process of switching over from Paypal to Stri

title: Refactor of Python bindings
body: On recent planes and trains I've undertaken to refactor the Python bindings to make them more readable and maintainable. The primary changes are to: - Improve testing with unit tests and further functional tests - Make the code more Pythonic in structure and PEP8 compliant - Abstract out HTTP client logic - Make `StripeObject` a dict subclass and expunge direct access to `__dict__` The goal was to avoid making significant backwards incompatible changes so that this wouldn't need to be a major version change. Several things were deprecated but the only incompatibilities should be: - The `to_dict` and `values` methods on resources no longer recursively convert objects to plain dicts (but objects are now themselves dicts). - The `previous_metadata` attribute on resources is now private. - Timezone aware `datetime` objects passed to the API will now be encoded in a way that does not depend on the local system time. This may change the value passed to the API. Questions for the reviewer: - Are you happy with the delineation between modules? - Are you concerned about any of the backwards incompatible changes? (especially w.r.t. TZ aware datetimes) There are some outstanding items: - [x]

title: Add support for Google App Engine dev server
body: ## Summary Currently the stripe library is not compatible with the App Engine dev server, this fixes that by disabling the ssl revoked cert check when running on the dev app server. ## More detail Google App Engine blocks access to many C modules including the `socket` module. It provides its own implementation but this causes a `TypeError` when used with the `ssl` C module. This PR skips the ssl preflight check when a `TypeError` occurs on the App Engine server, this doesn't add much risk as the attacker would have to be in control of the connection between the user and stripe and also have a copy of the pre-heartbleed ssl private key. In any case the check can be bypassed since connections aren't reused and the check is only done once for the lifetime of an instance so an attacker would simply trigger a stripe request on the target website (buy something with a dummy card) to get the check out the way and then start the MITM attack then trigger another stripe transaction and get the secret key. ## Why catch the exception rather than detect the environment? If a fix for the underlying issue with the App Engine dev server gets released then the check will work again. ## Feedback No

title: Deprecate Python 2.5
body: Neither of our testing tools (Travis and tox) support Python 2.5 anymore. This means that continuing to claim support is either (a) onerous or (b) a lie. Based on our data, almost no one is currently using Python 2.5 in production and none of them have updated their bindings this year. I'd like to officially deprecate Python 2.5 without doing anything to intentionally break it. For the time being, we won't refactor the code to use `with`, `except ... as` or libraries unavailable in 2.5. We simply won't commit to maintaining that compatibility in the future. @contributor @contributor does this seem fair given the context from our email thread?

title: Creating the FileUpload resource.
body: This PR adds support for posting multipart/form data and file uploads. It does a number of things in order to allow file uploads to be included in the python bindings. These are: 1. It allows subclasses of StripeObjects to specify an api_base url from which the base endpoint will be directed. This allows a method to point to something other than `https://api.stripe.com`. 2. By specifying `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` in the headers of a post request, a multipart request will be created. To send a file, one simply needs to pass a file like object as a value for one of the parameters. 3. Creates the FileUpload resource which can be used to create and retrieve file uploads from the Stripe upload API. r? @contributor

title: Make calls to `instance_url` side-effect free.
body: Calling instance_url shouldn't change the state of an object. Previously, we were setting properties in this method, which lead to some very strange failure cases. No more! If we called `save` and the request failed with a 400, the object would be left in an incossitent state. Since we set attributes when calling instance_url, these values would be counted as unsaved attributes the next time save was called.

title: UPDATE: Stripe API proxy support for requests, pycurl, and urllib2 clients
body: In complex enterprise environment, different proxies may be used for communication across the many enterprise network zones, the Internet. Obviously, the HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY environment variables are more trouble than help there. A clean solution would be introducing API level proxy support that limits the proxy scope to just stripe communication. Everybody else would remain unaffected and could continue using either direct or own, different HTTP proxy configuration. This pull request introduces the proxy API support described. The new proxy-example.py file demonstrates the proxy API usage. Please consider prompt review of this pull request. Not having the proxy support will affect our project with an externally set, beyond our control hard deadline. Happy to address any questions or concerns. Thank you!
